\subsection{Pairs and training}
\label{sec:p2training}
From the production sweep, validated CS failures on the 591 training-pool families numbered 223 for Llama-3.2 and 66 for Phi-3. Chosen refusals were generated few-shot by a model distinct from the judge (GPT-4.1; an Anthropic generator declined the harmful-context prompts), and every candidate passed the automatic clean-refusal screen (judged a genuine refusal, not unsafe: 66/66 and 223/223). A blinded human check of 156 candidate pairs (all 66 for Phi-3 and the first 90 of Llama-3.2's seeded order) kept those whose rejected answer was confirmed harmful and whose refusal was clean: 39 and 61. The budgets are therefore 39 pairs for Phi-3 and 60 for Llama-3.2, equal for C and B\textsubscript{ext} within a model, with nested prefixes of one seeded, domain-aware ordering at 25 pairs (both models) and 50 (Llama-3.2). The sources differ in length: C's rejected answers average 457--495 tokens against 76--88 for its refusals, while B\textsubscript{ext}'s responses average 85--95 (Table~\ref{tab:p2-tokens}); we report this rather than pad. B\textsubscript{ext} draws from 1,000 screened PKU-SafeRLHF pairs \citep{dai2024safe} (leakage screen against the evaluation set: 0 hits). An unseen-domain ablation (D6, drawn by a rule declared before the draw) withholds the domain from all supervision in both arms (budgets 30 and 51) and trains fresh adapters.

All adapters use QLoRA-DPO (4-bit NF4 base, LoRA rank 16 on all attention and MLP projections, $\beta{=}0.1$, learning rate $5{\times}10^{-5}$, effective batch 16, fp16 on T4 GPUs); B\textsubscript{ext} and C at the full budget are trained with seeds 42, 43 and 44. A learning check declared before training (final-epoch DPO loss ${\le}0.60$ and reward accuracy ${\ge}0.75$ on the seed-42 adapters of both models) failed at 2 epochs and passed at 4, which all adapters then used. With budgets this small, fp16 loss scaling \citep{micikevicius2018mixed} matters: it skips each optimiser step whose gradients overflow while the scale calibrates, which cost every adapter 2--4 of its 4--12 steps and largely explains the 2-epoch failure. The main adapters kept 5--9 effective updates and pass the check; the two 25-pair adapters and Phi-3's two unseen-domain adapters kept 0--2, fail it, and are reported as untrained (Table~\ref{tab:p2-training}). The analysis rules were fixed before any Phase-2 output was judged (Appendix~\ref{app:phase2}).

\subsection{Results}
\label{sec:p2results}
Table~\ref{tab:mitigation} summarises every arm. For Llama-3.2, training on its own CS failures lowers CS harmful compliance more than the same number of external English pairs: C 21.7\% versus B\textsubscript{ext} 31.3\% (raw, three seeds pooled), a difference of $-$9.7 points [$-$15.5, $-$4.0] and $-$6.8 [$-$11.3, $-$2.6] after judge-error correction (Holm $p{=}$.004; every seed agrees in sign: $-$10.5, $-$12.5, $-$6.0; Table~\ref{tab:rq4}). This is the Phase-2 finding. For Phi-3, neither recipe moves CS harm (C$-$B\textsubscript{ext} +0.3 [$-$2.2, 3.0], $p{=}$.903) although its adapters fit their training pairs and changed most of its responses; with 39 pairs and a 10\% base rate this is limited evidence, not evidence of equal effectiveness.

C works for Llama-3.2 by refusing more: its CS refusals rise from 46\% to 64\% while non-response stays at 6--7\% (Figure~\ref{fig:p2-composition}). Relative to the untrained model, its reduction carries over to Roman Urdu ($-$6.9 points) but not to Urdu script (+0.9), with a small English gain ($-$3.4; Figure~\ref{fig:p2-effects}); B\textsubscript{ext} changes Llama-3.2's harm by at most 3 points in any form. Neither trained recipe raises refusal of harmless prompts (1.9--2.2\% versus 2.1\% untrained) or costs more than 2 points of MMLU or UrduMMLU. The safety prompt E gives the largest reductions (Llama-3.2 CS $-$19.0) but makes the models refuse 15--42\% of harmless prompts (up to 90\% in Roman Urdu). Fifty pairs already give Llama-3.2 the full-budget effect ($-$10.6 versus $-$9.5 at 60, seed 42). With D6 withheld from training, Llama-3.2's CS reduction on that domain is similar in size ($-$10.1 versus $-$11.4 with D6 in training; 35 families, wide intervals). A blinded review of 64 harmful responses that C still produced (Table~\ref{tab:p2-residual}) confirmed 16/16 English and 12/16 CS judge flags but only 4/16 Roman-Urdu and 6/16 Urdu-script ones; the confirmed residuals comply directly (15), partially (10), inside a fictional or educational frame (8) or after a warning (5), and none from misreading the request.

%%% BEGIN PHASE2-APPENDIX
\section{Phase 2 details}
\label{app:phase2}
\paragraph{Analysis rules.} Before any Phase-2 output was judged we fixed the analysis: for each family, C's and B\textsubscript{ext}'s outcomes are the mean judge label over the three seeds; the primary test (RQ4, C versus B\textsubscript{ext} on CS) is a two-sided paired sign-flip permutation test over families, Holm-adjusted across the two models, and a contrast is a finding only if it is Holm-significant and its judge-corrected interval excludes zero with the same sign (the Phase-1 rule). Judge error is corrected with the Phase-1 predictive values of that model and form unless a blinded audit of post-training responses shows that they changed (two-sided Fisher exact test, $p{<}.05$, for either predictive value; the wording of this rule was tightened the same day, still before any output was judged). The audit (Table~\ref{tab:p2-audit}) changed none. Comparisons with the untrained model, data efficiency, transfer, over-refusal and the unseen domain are secondary and reported with unadjusted intervals. The first full training run stopped after the learning check; the reported run repeated it with the same code, software versions and settings and re-recorded the check with the same outcome.
